A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study by Plaut, Khanh, and Trinh. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial methodological and presentation revisions.

before.justification: V3 reports original calibration, correctness-prediction, and abstention experiments on 15 chat LLMs, with additional prompting and token-aggregation analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: V4 reports original chat-model experiments and adds base-model results, alternative uncertainty measures, post-hoc calibration, and expanded training-sample-size analyses.

M1.justification: V3 generates a response greedily, parses its answer letter, and takes that token's probability and logit. V4 instead selects the highest-scoring allowed answer token at the first usable response position and renormalizes probabilities across answer options (Section 3). This changes both answer selection and the uncertainty scores used throughout the study.

E1.justification: Both versions use ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, MMLU, TruthfulQA, and WinoGrande for multiple-choice Q&A and abstention, retaining zero-shot and five-shot prompting. The additions concern model configurations and analyses of retained coverage, rather than new datasets, domains, or tasks.

E2.justification: V4 adds evaluated entropy, probability-margin, and logit-margin alternatives to MSP and Max Logit (Appendix C), plus comparisons with Platt-scaled probabilities (Appendix D). V3's product-of-token-probabilities alternative is removed. The abstention baseline labeled 'Base' in v3 is retained as 'No abstain' in v4.

E3.justification: V4 adds the 13 open-weight base checkpoints to the experimental design and revises answer extraction and normalization. Section 6.1 changes the stated threshold-training sample from k questions to k per dataset, explicitly pooling 5k questions for one threshold per model. Appendix A.1 also changes calibration-curve balancing from approximate duplication to exactly 6,000 observations per dataset through additional sampling. These are reported protocol revisions.

E4.justification: V4 tests sensitivity to entropy and margin scores, learned and manually chosen Platt-scaling parameters, and five-shot prompting for base models. Threshold-training sensitivity expands from v3's k=10 and half-data tables to curves spanning k=1–500 per dataset. The product-of-token-probabilities analysis and comparison of duplicated versus unweighted calibration curves are removed.

E5.justification: The Mann–Whitney tests and their 10^-4 threshold remain. The stated cross-model testing family changes from eight comparisons with an approximately 0.006 threshold to 18 comparisons with a conservative 10^-3 threshold. Cross-model summaries switch from Pearson r to R-squared. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, seeds, or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: Accuracy, calibration, AUROC, abstention scores, and correlations are extensively revised. For example, SOLAR 10.7B's MSP AUROC is 59.7 in v3 Table 1 and 71.8 in v4 Table 2, under the changed scoring procedure; this is not a same-setting performance gain. V4 adds base-model, alternative-score, calibration, and sample-size results, while removing product-MSP results and per-dataset abstention-frequency tables.

T1.justification: The formal MSP and Max Logit definitions change from vocabulary-wide maxima to answer-token maxima, including an explicit answer-set normalization denominator for MSP. Appendix D adds a parameterized Platt-scaling definition. Its printed formula decreases with the input for the positive A values reported in Figure 17, conflicting with the order-preservation explanation. No substantial theorem or proof development is added.

C1.justification: The three central chat-model findings remain, but v4 adds a base-versus-chat contrast to the introduction, summary Table 1, and conclusion. V3 explicitly says its experiments cannot determine fine-tuning's impact; v4 concludes that its results pinpoint chat fine-tuning as the source of the calibration/correctness-prediction divergence. V4 also explicitly presents miscalibration as corroborating prior work.

C2.justification: V4 adds explanations involving recalibration and preserved score ordering, interprets logit margin as a form of normalization, and argues that very frequent abstention can be appropriate for unreliable models. It replaces the base-model-exclusion limitation with cautions about tiny unnormalized answer probabilities and acknowledges that the base-model calibration correlation misses its adjusted significance threshold. These are substantive additions to mechanisms and qualifications.

D1.justification: V4 replaces the supplementary-code statement with a repository link, documents the dummy-token exception and Platt-parameter fitting, and updates reported computation from about 1,000 to 2,000 GPU-hours and API cost from about $120 to $110. V3's license and dataset-content documentation is removed. The PDFs establish changes in disclosure, without verifying the linked resource externally.

R1.justification: Related work substantially expands around post-hoc calibration, verbalized uncertainty, and answer-token evaluation, adding works such as Shen et al. (2024), Xie et al. (2024), and Xiao et al. (2025). The abstract and introduction more clearly distinguish reproduced calibration findings from the contribution of comprehensive cross-model comparisons.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, and score-computation explanation are extensively rewritten. Dataset difficulty, model-size correlations, and prompt-phrasing discussion move from Appendix A into Section 5.2. Limitations are integrated into the conclusion, an author-contributions statement is added, and the appendices are reorganized around the expanded analyses.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to a single-column journal layout. V3 Figures 2 and 3 become the paired panels of v4 Figure 2, with revised legend placement. V4 adds a summary table and numerous base-model, uncertainty, calibration, and sensitivity displays, relocates existing analyses into the main text, and reorganizes the dataset-level presentation.

improvement.justification: V4 supplies base-model controls absent from v3, tests alternative uncertainty measures, and clarifies the relationship to prior work, improving evidential support and positioning. The net gain is limited by overstatement and new inconsistencies: Section 6.2 claims improvement in all conditions although Table 4 gives Llama 3.1 8B a balanced Max Logit score of 20.5 versus 23.9 without abstention. Appendix D's Platt formula also reverses ordering for Figure 17's reported positive A values, weakening confidence in that added analysis.
